title: A one-second difference you can inspect
status: WIP study; reported results, not independently rerun for this website
tolerance: 0.05 of the profile's unit (A or W)

claims.statement: Three rules of the reference program
claims.boundary: About the Lean model, not a proof of EVerest's implementation.
claims.summary: Three rules proved about the model

claims.boundary: All 2,000 pass; 57,304 instants with a model limit agree within tolerance, and neither program gives a limit at the other 10,226 instants.
835 pass, 92 warn, 1,073 fail, as reported. The report also records 1,081 instants with an extra EVerest limit; see the classification caveat.

results.configuration: Older anchors, shifted by leap seconds

classificationCaveat: The pinned report is internally inconsistent about extra limits: its updated Q4 header calls an EVerest limit where the model has none a warning, while a retained note says these instants were unclassified. Its counters record 1,081 such instants in the older run. The totals here are the report's published totals, not a reconstruction or a new run. A pass is not a general claim of exact agreement.

witness.profile: One daily TxDefaultProfile on connector 0, stack level 3, with no duration
witness.severity: Low, as rated by the study; one to three seconds of drift in the reported examples.

modelProperties: The combined limit is never above the charger-wide limit.
It is never above the applicable transaction limit.
While a transaction's own schedule applies, changing default schedules does not change the limit.
unfinishedProperty: Adding a lower-priority schedule that does not apply leaves the limit unchanged (I4).
humanDecisions: The owner approved interpretations A1 and A2 and reclassified two AI correspondence-review findings as abstractions rather than approximations.
The owner confirmed restoring the missing s ≤ t condition in D4 on 2026-10-27.
Q4 treats lower limits as conforming; the owner chose to warn about lost charging. The report retains the classification caveat recorded here.
trustedDependencies: Lean v4.28.0 and its standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for the stated completed proofs.
The reviewed interpretation of OCPP 1.6 edition 2 and the Lean model's correspondence to it.
The C++ compiler, driver, copied installation/orchestration glue, two shim headers, Python harness, JSON adapter and model runner.
The operating system timezone database read by the driver; its leap-second table must contain exactly the three leap seconds since 2010 (2012-06-30, 2015-06-30, 2016-12-31).

environment.compiler: Apple clang 21.0.0, C++17; reported on macOS arm64
otherPrerequisites: elan with the Lean toolchain installed
environment.boundary: Source and downloaded inputs are pinned. The host compiler, system headers and timezone database still need matching; this is not a hermetically pinned environment.

coverage: At most 2 charger-wide, 3 default and 2 transaction profiles, up to 4 periods per profile, 15-minute offsets, 24- or 48-hour windows in 2026, on connector 1. Absolute, daily and weekly schedules are generated. Each case samples transition instants from either program and one second either side.

notYetReached.blocker: No transaction start time in the model
notYetReached.question: How should transaction-relative time enter the model?

notYetReached.blocker: One scalar limit and no phase count
notYetReached.question: How should phase-dependent limits be represented?
What assumptions justify conversion between units?
How should the station-wide sum be constrained?
How should connectivity change profile selection?

notYetReached.blocker: No transaction ID field or active-transaction input
notYetReached.question: How should transaction identity constrain applicability?

notYetReached.blocker: Different profile structure and separate production code
notYetReached.question: Which rules and model changes are needed for OCPP 2.x?

ambiguity: Default profiles on connectors 0 and 1 together are not generated: the signed spec leaves their interaction unresolved. The recurrence wording also admits another interpretation; the study records it as OCA note N4.
upstreamStatus: The pinned study contains a draft EVerest issue awaiting human review. It records no upstream filing. This website does not submit one.
replayNote: The older-anchor run is expected to report failures; a nonzero exit is a reproduced finding, not an installation failure. --leap-correct changes input anchors for diagnosis and does not fix EVerest. A run writes drt_report_latest.md; preserve the pinned historical report.
publicationNote: This editorial snapshot summarizes linked historical evidence. It is not evidence-record/1, an automatic attestation, a new experimental run, or independent proof rechecking.

contribution.summary: I built Crosscheck to make claims about AI-written code inspectable. For this study, I used its AI-assisted workflow to model OCPP 1.6 charging schedules and compare the model with EVerest's scheduling code.
contribution.human: I directed the study, approved interpretations of the charging rules, reviewed correspondence findings and decided which claims the evidence supports. The signed spec and owner decisions record that judgment.
contribution.agents: AI agents drafted specifications, Lean code, proof attempts and test tooling. An AI correspondence review searched for mismatches. Its verdicts needed review; they do not count as evidence.
contribution.checks: Lean checks the completed proofs about the model. A differential harness compares generated inputs with EVerest's unmodified scheduling code through a driver. The compiler, model interpretation, driver and harness remain trusted dependencies.
contribution.result: The study reports a low-severity recurrence drift caused by leap seconds, with a concrete witness and diagnostic reruns. It does not establish a deployed fix, full OCPP conformance or a proof of the production implementation.

engineeringDecisions.choice: Separate the model from the production implementation
engineeringDecisions.reason: A Lean reference program lets the study state and prove model properties, then compare its answers with the existing C++ implementation.
engineeringDecisions.boundary: A proof about that model does not establish correspondence with all production behavior.

engineeringDecisions.choice: Check the moments where schedules change
engineeringDecisions.reason: The harness compares transition instants from either program and one second either side. That makes a one-second timing difference visible.
engineeringDecisions.boundary: The generator still has bounded profiles, periods and time windows; agreement does not cover other inputs.

engineeringDecisions.choice: Record interpretation decisions before judging differences
engineeringDecisions.reason: The owner resolved ambiguities in the signed spec and reviewed the correspondence findings against those decisions.
engineeringDecisions.boundary: A difference caused by a disputed reading of the standard must remain distinct from an implementation defect.

engineeringDecisions.choice: Publish the limits beside the result
engineeringDecisions.reason: The study keeps the unfinished fourth proof, trusted dependencies and classification inconsistency visible, with pinned replay inputs.
engineeringDecisions.boundary: The leap-second input shift is a diagnostic experiment, not an upstream repair.
